requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The only source change is in TypeCollector.cs, in both member loops (properties and fields). After the mixed int/string key diagnostic is reported, the offending member is now skipped with `continue`. Before this, the code went on to `intKey!.Value` or `ContainsKey(null)` and threw. Members with a duplicate int or string key are now added to the member dictionaries only once, so `Dictionary.Add` no longer throws after MsgPack005 is reported. Alongside this, the change adds eight analyzer tests for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types, two execution tests, and a README section describing which diagnostics apply to suppressed types.
story.why: The issue says the analyzer stops working for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types since 3.1.1. The change treats an exception thrown inside TypeCollector as the cause. Such an exception aborts the analyzer and swallows all its diagnostics. Nothing in the diff touches code that checks `SuppressSourceGeneration`. The fix is generic: it applies to generated types as well, as one of the new tests shows.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section that documents analyzer behaviour, including MsgPack012, which no test covers.
An execution test project file adds a test type and two runtime tests; one of them asserts nothing about the suppressed type.
The duplicate-key and mixed-key guards also change behaviour for normal, non-suppressed `[MessagePackObject]` types.
story.confidence_overview: High: the duplicate and mixed-key guards in the property loop stop the crash, because the verifier would fail on an analyzer exception and the tests target exactly these cases. Low to medium: whether this is the actual 3.1.1 regression from the issue. No suppression-specific code changed, and several new tests (MsgPack004/015/003) may already have passed before the change. The field-loop edits have no direct test. The execution 'no formatter generated' test checks nothing.
